fatal_errors: It identifies conventional tempered martensitic steel rather than the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy.
It substitutes classical impurity-segregation temper embrittlement for the target mechanism involving enhanced L12 ordering, planar slip, and jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
It conflates aging temperature with mechanical test temperature and does not reproduce the approximately 600°C embrittlement and 750°C recovery treatments.
It explicitly claims that high-entropy alloys will not exhibit the transition, directly contradicting the reported result.
No supporting evidence is provided for the proposed material or temperature-dependent sequence.
explanation: The hypothesis captures only the generic shape of a ductile-brittle-ductile response. It instead restates the conventional temper-embrittlement baseline that the context contrasts with the new finding. The target is an as-cast FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA whose ductility is minimized after aging near 600°C because L12 ordering raises antiphase-boundary energy and promotes planar slip, while jagged B2/FCC boundaries concentrate stress and initiate instability. Ductility recovers near 750°C as ordering is reduced and ductile transition zones develop along phase boundaries. The proposed experiment could test impurity segregation in steel, but it would not discriminate or validate the target ordering/phase-boundary mechanism.
